subproblem.title: Graph planes q(graph A): fixed vectors (P1), normal estimate (Nor), the bounded graph parametrization and the difference identity
subproblem.statement: For all n, l and every linear isometry (linear isometric equivalence) q of R^(n+l) = Amb n l. Here graphPoint(a, b) in R^(n+l) has first n coordinates a in R^n and last l coordinates b in R^l, and ||.|| is the operator norm. For continuous linear A : R^n -> R^l let G_A := q(span{graphPoint(v, A v) : v in R^n}), the submodule Submodule.map q (span (range (v -> graphPoint v (A v)))), and let P_A be its orthogonal projection (starProjection). Then: (P1) P_A(q(graphPoint(x, A x))) = q(graphPoint(x, A x)) for every x in R^n; (P2) |w| <= (1 + ||A||^2)^(1/2) |q(graphPoint(0, w)) - P_A q(graphPoint(0, w))| for every w in R^l; (W) there is a continuous linear W : R^n -> R^(n+l) with W v = q(graphPoint(v, A v)) for all v in R^n and ||W|| <= (1 + ||A||^2)^(1/2); (D) for continuous linear A, B : R^n -> R^l and v in R^n, q(graphPoint(v, A v)) - q(graphPoint(v, B v)) = q(graphPoint(0, (A - B) v)).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (n ℓ : ℕ) (q : Amb n ℓ ≃ₗᵢ[ℝ] Amb n ℓ), (∀ (A : Rn n →L[ℝ] Rn ℓ) (x : Rn n), (Submodule.map q.toLinearEquiv.toLinearMap (Submodule.span ℝ (Set.range fun v : Rn n => graphPoint v (A v)))).starProjection (q (graphPoint x (A x))) = q (graphPoint x (A x))) ∧ (∀ (A : Rn n →L[ℝ] Rn ℓ) (w : Rn ℓ), ‖w‖ ≤ Real.sqrt (1 + ‖A‖ ^ 2) * ‖q (graphPoint (0 : Rn n) w) - (Submodule.map q.toLinearEquiv.toLinearMap (Submodule.span ℝ (Set.range fun v : Rn n => graphPoint v (A v)))).starProjection (q (graphPoint (0 : Rn n) w))‖) ∧ (∀ A : Rn n →L[ℝ] Rn ℓ, ∃ W : Rn n →L[ℝ] Amb n ℓ, (∀ v : Rn n, W v = q (graphPoint v (A v))) ∧ ‖W‖ ≤ Real.sqrt (1 + ‖A‖ ^ 2)) ∧ ∀ (A B : Rn n →L[ℝ] Rn ℓ) (v : Rn n), q (graphPoint v (A v)) - q (graphPoint v (B v)) = q (graphPoint (0 : Rn n) ((A - B) v))
subproblem.natural_proof:
Notation.
- N := n + l, so Amb n l = R^N. Every index of Fin N is exactly one of Fin.castAdd l i (i < n) or Fin.natAdd n j (j < l).
- By definition graphPoint a b = toLp(Fin.append a b), so (graphPoint a b)_{castAdd l i} = a_i and (graphPoint a b)_{natAdd n j} = b_j.
- q is linear and |q z| = |z| for all z. ||.|| is the operator norm.
- This proof uses only the frozen contract, not la_basics. Steps 1-2 re-derive the coordinate facts it needs.

1. Coordinate algebra. Two vectors of R^N are equal iff their coordinates agree at every castAdd l i and every natAdd n j (Fin.addCases). Comparing coordinates (a_i + a'_i, b_j + b'_j, and so on):
(G1) graphPoint(a + a', b + b') = graphPoint(a, b) + graphPoint(a', b');
(G2) graphPoint(a - a', b - b') = graphPoint(a, b) - graphPoint(a', b');
(G3) graphPoint(t a, t b) = t graphPoint(a, b) for real t.
(G4) Split the sum in |z|^2 = sum_k z_k^2 over Fin (n + l) into its castAdd and natAdd parts (Fin.sum_univ_add):
|graphPoint(a, b)|^2 = sum_{i<n} a_i^2 + sum_{j<l} b_j^2 = |a|^2 + |b|^2.

2. The graph map. Fix A and define g_A : R^n -> R^N by g_A(v) := graphPoint(v, A v).
- g_A is linear: g_A(v + v') = graphPoint(v + v', A v + A v') = g_A(v) + g_A(v') by linearity of A and (G1), and g_A(t v) = graphPoint(t v, t A v) = t g_A(v) by (G3).
- So its range is a linear subspace. The span of a subspace is itself: span(range g_A) = range g_A (Submodule.span_eq with LinearMap.coe_range).
- Consequently every element of G_A = q(range g_A) has the form q(graphPoint(v, A v)) for some v in R^n.

3. (P1). graphPoint(x, A x) = g_A(x) lies in range g_A, which is contained in its span. So q(graphPoint(x, A x)) lies in G_A (Submodule.mem_map_of_mem). An orthogonal projection fixes exactly the vectors of its subspace (starProjection_eq_self_iff), so P_A(q(graphPoint(x, A x))) = q(graphPoint(x, A x)).

4. (P2). Let y := q(graphPoint(0, w)).
(i) P_A y lies in G_A (starProjection_apply_mem), so by step 2 P_A y = q(graphPoint(v, A v)) for some v in R^n.
(ii) By linearity of q and (G2): y - P_A y = q(graphPoint(0, w) - graphPoint(v, A v)) = q(graphPoint(0 - v, w - A v)).
(iii) By the isometry property and (G4): |y - P_A y|^2 = |-v|^2 + |w - A v|^2 = |v|^2 + |w - A v|^2, i.e. |y - P_A y| = (|v|^2 + |w - A v|^2)^(1/2).
(iv) Put a := |w - A v|, b := |v|, c := ||A||, all >= 0. By the triangle inequality and |A v| <= ||A|| |v|: |w| = |(w - A v) + A v| <= a + |A v| <= a + c b.
(v) Cauchy-Schwarz in R^2: (1 + c^2)(a^2 + b^2) - (a + c b)^2 = (c a - b)^2 >= 0. Since a + c b >= 0, taking square roots gives a + c b <= ((1 + c^2)(b^2 + a^2))^(1/2) = (1 + c^2)^(1/2) (b^2 + a^2)^(1/2).
By (iii)-(v), |w| <= (1 + ||A||^2)^(1/2) |y - P_A y|, which is (P2).

5. (W). Let W := q o g_A : R^n -> R^N.
- W is linear (a composition of linear maps). It is continuous because R^n is finite-dimensional (LinearMap.toContinuousLinearMap) and q is continuous.
- W v = q(graphPoint(v, A v)) by definition.
- For every v, by the isometry property, (G4), |A v| <= ||A|| |v| and monotonicity of the square root:
|W v| = |graphPoint(v, A v)| = (|v|^2 + |A v|^2)^(1/2) <= ((1 + ||A||^2)|v|^2)^(1/2) = (1 + ||A||^2)^(1/2) |v|.
- Since (1 + ||A||^2)^(1/2) >= 0, the definition of the operator norm (ContinuousLinearMap.opNorm_le_bound) gives ||W|| <= (1 + ||A||^2)^(1/2).

6. (D). By linearity of q, (G2), v - v = 0 and (A - B) v = A v - B v:
q(graphPoint(v, A v)) - q(graphPoint(v, B v)) = q(graphPoint(v, A v) - graphPoint(v, B v)) = q(graphPoint(v - v, A v - B v)) = q(graphPoint(0, (A - B) v)).

7. Steps 3-6 prove the four conjuncts for all n, l, q and every A (and B).
proof_key_steps: Coordinate algebra of graphPoint: additivity, subtraction, homogeneity, and |graphPoint(a, b)|^2 = |a|^2 + |b|^2
v -> graphPoint(v, A v) is linear, so span(range) = range and G_A = {q(graphPoint(v, A v)) : v}
(P1): q(graphPoint(x, A x)) lies in G_A and is fixed by P_A
(P2): P_A y = q(graphPoint(v, A v)), |y - P_A y|^2 = |v|^2 + |w - A v|^2, then the triangle inequality and (a + c b)^2 <= (1 + c^2)(a^2 + b^2)
(W): W = q o g_A is continuous linear with |W v|^2 = |v|^2 + |A v|^2 <= (1 + ||A||^2)|v|^2
(D): linearity of q and graphPoint subtraction

audit.reason: The type exactly expresses P1, P2, W and D with the stated isometric equivalence and continuous linear maps. Coordinate algebra establishes the graph range and norm decomposition; membership proves P1; the explicit square calculation proves P2 with justified nonnegativity; finite-dimensional continuity and the pointwise bound establish W; subtraction proves D. No smallness hypothesis, positive dimension, la_basics result or parent theorem is implicitly required.

subproblem.title: Hilbert-Schmidt norm: transposition invariance and the two-sided operator-ideal bounds
subproblem.statement: For all natural numbers m, k, p, write R^m = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin m) (Rn m) with standard basis e_i = EuclideanSpace.single i 1. For a continuous linear X : R^m -> R^k let hsNormSq X = sum_{i<m} |X e_i|^2. Let <.,.> be the Euclidean inner product and ||.|| the operator norm. Then: (H1) if X : R^m -> R^k and Y : R^k -> R^m are continuous linear maps with <X u, v> = <u, Y v> for all u in R^m and v in R^k (i.e. Y is an adjoint of X), then hsNormSq Y = hsNormSq X; (H2) for continuous linear Y : R^k -> R^p and X : R^m -> R^k, hsNormSq (Y o X) <= ||Y||^2 hsNormSq X; (H3) for continuous linear X : R^m -> R^k and W : R^p -> R^m, hsNormSq (X o W) <= ||W||^2 hsNormSq X.
subproblem.lean_statement: (∀ (m k : ℕ) (X : Rn m →L[ℝ] Rn k) (Y : Rn k →L[ℝ] Rn m), (∀ (u : Rn m) (v : Rn k), inner ℝ (X u) v = inner ℝ u (Y v)) → hsNormSq Y = hsNormSq X) ∧ (∀ (m k p : ℕ) (Y : Rn k →L[ℝ] Rn p) (X : Rn m →L[ℝ] Rn k), hsNormSq (Y ∘L X) ≤ ‖Y‖ ^ 2 * hsNormSq X) ∧ ∀ (m k p : ℕ) (X : Rn m →L[ℝ] Rn k) (W : Rn p →L[ℝ] Rn m), hsNormSq (X ∘L W) ≤ ‖W‖ ^ 2 * hsNormSq X
subproblem.natural_proof:
Notation.
- e_i (i < m), f_j (j < k), g_r (r < p) are the standard basis vectors EuclideanSpace.single _ 1 of R^m, R^k, R^p.
- z_j is the j-th coordinate of a vector z, <.,.> the real Euclidean inner product, ||.|| the operator norm.
- o is composition of continuous linear maps (∘L).

1. Coordinates. For z in R^k:
- |z|^2 = sum_{j<k} z_j^2 (EuclideanSpace.real_norm_sq_eq);
- <z, f_j> = z_j = <f_j, z> (EuclideanSpace.inner_single_right and inner_single_left with a = 1).
The same holds in R^m and R^p.

2. (H1). Fix i < m and j < k. By step 1 and the hypothesis with u = e_i, v = f_j:
(X e_i)_j = <X e_i, f_j> = <e_i, Y f_j> = (Y f_j)_i.
Hence, by step 1 and exchanging the two finite sums:
hsNormSq X = sum_{i<m} |X e_i|^2
= sum_{i<m} sum_{j<k} (X e_i)_j^2
= sum_{i<m} sum_{j<k} (Y f_j)_i^2
= sum_{j<k} sum_{i<m} (Y f_j)_i^2
= sum_{j<k} |Y f_j|^2
= hsNormSq Y.

3. (H2). Fix i < m.
- (Y o X) e_i = Y(X e_i), and |Y(X e_i)| <= ||Y|| |X e_i| by the definition of the operator norm (ContinuousLinearMap.le_opNorm).
- Both sides are >= 0, so |Y(X e_i)|^2 <= ||Y||^2 |X e_i|^2.
Summing over i < m: hsNormSq (Y o X) <= ||Y||^2 sum_{i<m} |X e_i|^2 = ||Y||^2 hsNormSq X.

4. Adjoints. Every continuous linear T : R^a -> R^b has a continuous linear adjoint T* : R^b -> R^a with <T u, v> = <u, T* v> for all u, v, and ||T*|| <= ||T||.
- Construction: T* v := sum_{i<a} <T e_i, v> e_i. It is linear in v, hence continuous (finite dimension). For u = sum_i u_i e_i, linearity of T gives <u, T* v> = sum_i u_i <T e_i, v> = <T u, v>.
- Bound: by the identity with u = T* v and Cauchy-Schwarz, |T* v|^2 = <T* v, T* v> = <T(T* v), v> <= ||T|| |T* v| |v|. So |T* v| <= ||T|| |v| (trivial if T* v = 0), i.e. ||T*|| <= ||T||.
- In Lean this is Mathlib's ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint, used with ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint_inner_right. It is a linear isometric equivalence, so even ||T*|| = ||T|| (LinearIsometryEquiv.norm_map).
- The frozen contract does not import it, so the proof adds import Mathlib.Analysis.InnerProductSpace.Adjoint. The statement itself mentions no adjoint.

5. (H3). Let X* : R^k -> R^m and W* : R^m -> R^p be adjoints of X and W as in step 4.
(a) For u in R^p and v in R^k:
<(X o W) u, v> = <X(W u), v> = <W u, X* v> = <u, W*(X* v)> = <u, (W* o X*) v>.
By (H1) for the pair (X o W, W* o X*), maps R^p -> R^k and R^k -> R^p: hsNormSq (W* o X*) = hsNormSq (X o W).

subproblem.statement: For all n, l, every linear isometry (linear isometric equivalence) q of R^(n+l) = Amb n l, and all continuous linear A, B : R^n -> R^l: let P_A and P_B be the orthogonal projections (starProjection) of R^(n+l) onto G_A = q(span{graphPoint(v, A v) : v in R^n}) and G_B = q(span{graphPoint(v, B v) : v in R^n}). Then 2 hsNormSq(A - B) <= (1 + ||A||^2)(1 + ||B||^2) hsNormSq(P_A - P_B). Here hsNormSq M = sum_i |M e_i|^2 over the standard basis of the domain of M (for P_A - P_B, the standard basis of R^(n+l)), and ||.|| is the operator norm.

- N := n + l, so Amb n l = R^N = Rn N, and hsNormSq of a map of R^N is computed in the standard basis of R^N.
- For continuous linear C : R^n -> R^l, P_C is the orthogonal projection onto G_C := q(span{graphPoint(v, C v) : v in R^n}).
- e_i (i < n) is the standard basis of R^n; o is composition.

Cited sibling results:
- hs_ideal (H3): for continuous linear X : R^a -> R^b and W : R^c -> R^a, hsNormSq(X o W) <= ||W||^2 hsNormSq X.
- hs_proj_split (S2): for subspaces K, L of R^a, hsNormSq(P_K - P_L) = hsNormSq((P_K - P_L) o P_K) + hsNormSq((P_K - P_L) o P_L).
- graph_param, for this q and all continuous linear C, D:
  - (P1) P_C(q(graphPoint(x, C x))) = q(graphPoint(x, C x));
  - (P2) |w| <= (1 + ||C||^2)^(1/2) |q(graphPoint(0, w)) - P_C q(graphPoint(0, w))|;
  - (W) there is a continuous linear W : R^n -> R^N with W v = q(graphPoint(v, C v)) and ||W|| <= (1 + ||C||^2)^(1/2);

0. Elementary facts.
(a) hsNormSq M >= 0 for every M (a sum of squares).
(b) hsNormSq(-M) = hsNormSq M, since |(-M) e_i| = |M e_i|.

1. One-sided estimate. For every ordered pair (C, D) of continuous linear maps R^n -> R^l:
hsNormSq(C - D) <= (1 + ||C||^2)(1 + ||D||^2) hsNormSq((P_C - P_D) o P_C).
Proof. Put Z := P_C - P_D and choose W for C by (W). Since 0 <= ||W|| <= (1 + ||C||^2)^(1/2), we have ||W||^2 <= 1 + ||C||^2.
(i) Fix i < n and put e := e_i and y := q(graphPoint(0, (C - D) e)).
- By (D), W e = q(graphPoint(e, C e)) = q(graphPoint(e, D e)) + y.
- By (P1) for C, P_C(W e) = W e.
- By (P1) for D and linearity of P_D, P_D(W e) = q(graphPoint(e, D e)) + P_D y.
Hence (Z o W) e = P_C(W e) - P_D(W e) = q(graphPoint(e, D e)) + y - q(graphPoint(e, D e)) - P_D y = y - P_D y.
(ii) By (P2) for D with w := (C - D) e:
|(C - D) e| <= (1 + ||D||^2)^(1/2) |y - P_D y| = (1 + ||D||^2)^(1/2) |(Z o W) e|.
Both sides are >= 0, so squaring gives |(C - D) e_i|^2 <= (1 + ||D||^2) |(Z o W) e_i|^2. Summing over i < n:
hsNormSq(C - D) <= (1 + ||D||^2) hsNormSq(Z o W).
(iii) By (P1) for C, P_C(W v) = W v for every v, so Z o W = (Z o P_C) o W. Apply (H3) with X := Z o P_C (a map R^N -> R^N) and W : R^n -> R^N, then use ||W||^2 <= 1 + ||C||^2 and 0(a):
hsNormSq(Z o W) = hsNormSq((Z o P_C) o W) <= ||W||^2 hsNormSq(Z o P_C) <= (1 + ||C||^2) hsNormSq(Z o P_C).
(iv) Multiply (iii) by 1 + ||D||^2 >= 0 and combine with (ii):
hsNormSq(C - D) <= (1 + ||D||^2)(1 + ||C||^2) hsNormSq(Z o P_C) = (1 + ||C||^2)(1 + ||D||^2) hsNormSq((P_C - P_D) o P_C).

2. Put c := (1 + ||A||^2)(1 + ||B||^2). Step 1 for (C, D) = (A, B) gives hsNormSq(A - B) <= c hsNormSq((P_A - P_B) o P_A).
